chunks: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) said: In Paradise there is a gate called the Gate of the Strivers. They will proceed toward it, and it will be open, while they are girded with their swords -- and the assembly gathered at the standing place -- and the angels welcome them.
Whoever abandons jihad, Allah will clothe him in humiliation within himself, poverty in his livelihood, and effacement of his religion.
Indeed, Allah, blessed and exalted, has given glory to my nation through the hooves of its horses and the posts of its spears.

key_terms.الجهاد: Jihad: striving in the way of Allah, encompassing armed struggle, spiritual effort, and enjoining good
key_terms.المجاهدين: The mujahidin: those who strive in the way of Allah, whether through armed defense or spiritual exertion
key_terms.سنابك: Sanabik: hooves of horses (plural of sunbuk), symbolizing military might
key_terms.محقا: Mahq: effacement, annihilation, gradual destruction of something

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad say about the Gate of the Mujahidin in Paradise?
ai.summary: The Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) describes a special gate in Paradise reserved for the mujahidin, who will arrive armed and be welcomed by angels. He warns that abandoning jihad brings threefold punishment: personal humiliation, economic poverty, and spiritual decline. This teaching was delivered in the context of early Islamic society where communal defense was essential for the survival of the Muslim community, and 'jihad' encompassed both military defense and spiritual striving.
